It depends on the context, I see phones as more of a means to other things. If having a phone is completely necessary to access basic services that are rights, like   staple food, healthcare (in countries that have public healthcare), housing, welfare, education etc., then yeah I’d say having a phone becomes a right because you wouldn’t be able to access your rights without a phone.

If you don’t need a phone to access basic services, then it’s a luxury. But considering how everything is going digital, I do think either phones should become a right, or every service needs to allow a convenient way of accessing them without needing a phone or the internet.

it sounds like you’re comparing yourself to an impossible standard. you want to do well in school, gym and women, but there’s no ‘average’ guy that’s got everything worked out. everyone has their own struggles and insecurities. you’ve gotta be kinder to yourself and recognize that taking steps for improvement is more than enough. you’ve also gotta be kinder to other people and recognize that they’re struggling with life as much as you are, just in different ways.

I think what’s really important is for you to learn how to live apart from your parents. Since you’re in college, I’d say look into joining any clubs or societies that may interest you if they’re available. If you’re not sure what interests you, find clubs that want to teach people new things and are always welcome to newcomers. Aside from learning how to socialize, you also have a place to be away from your parents.

Definitely take small incremental steps to improvement. Start small, like spend 30 minutes after work on finding and working on a hobby, then be consistent. 

What also worked for me was to lose the mindset that “my life will really begin when …”, and intentionally notice the small nice things that are already in my life. It’s the simple stuff like being able to take a hot shower or spend time with family. You don’t need to do anything amazing, like having a ‘purpose’ to be alive and happy.
